new.st: The U.S. Treasure Atlas vol. 5 lists Herold, 2.5 miles east of Alma, as a ghost town. GNIS places it (1566324), and the 1877 plat book draws a church in sec. 16 and a school in sec. 9, both already pinned 150-300 m from here. Herold Cemetery is next to the pin.

new.pl: On the east county line, about 7 miles northeast of Independence

new.st: The U.S. Treasure Atlas vol. 5 lists Theisen, on the east county line 7 miles northeast of Independence, as a ghost town. The 1878 Buffalo County map labels Theisen Creek here, with a church about 1 km west in sec. 11; the 1877 plat church pin in sec. 11 T22N R10W is 760 m from this pin.
new.t: Church lot first; a cemetery, if any, is look-only. Private land: permission first.

t-tr-le-sueur.t: The fort ground is on the hillside behind locked gates (private). The big grass meadow between the road and the hill, running to the river, is said to be county park land: get written OK from Blue Earth County Parks before detecting. The river edge at low water is the other target.
